ta: கார் மேனி செங்கண் கதிர் மதியம் போல் முகத்தான்
en: Āl! O those who have proceeded to bathe in the month of Mārkaḻi
on a good day filled with a full moon!
O ladies adorned with fine jewels! Will you not go [with me]?
O you wealthy girls from the cowherds’ hamlet/Gokula abounding with prosperity!
The Son of Nandagopa with a sharp spear [and] a cruel occupation
The young Lion of Yaśoda with beautiful eyes
[with] a cloud[-like] body, red eyes
[and] with a face like the sun [and] the moon, Nārāyaṇa Himself
will give the paṟai-drum solely to us!
Bathe, so that the people of the world praise [us]
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: pronominalised noun, vocative, honorific, second person
pronominalised noun, masculine singular, third person
pronominalised noun, feminine singular, third person
pronominalised noun, masculine singular, third person

en: O those who live on [this] earth!
Won’t you listen [about] the rites that we are going to perform for our Pāvai[-vow]?
Singing about the feet of the Supreme Being who gently slept on the milk ocean
We shall not eat ghee
we shall not drink milk
Bathing in the early morning
We shall not paint [our eyes] using kohl
We shall not adorn [our hair] placing flowers
We shall not do that which is not [to be] done
We shall not go and speak evil calumny
Giving a little alms [and] food charity as much as possible
Pondering on the path to redemption
[we shall] rejoice
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: participial noun, vocative, plural, second person
participial noun, neuter plural, negative, third person

ta: தீங்கின்றி நாடெல்லாம் திங்கள் மும் மாரி பெய்து
ஓங்கு பெரும் செந் நெல் ஊடு கயலுகளப்
பூங்குவளைப் போதில் பொறி வண்டு கண் படுப்பத்
வாங்க குடம் நிறைக்கும் வள்ளல் பெரும் பசுக்கள்
en: If — singing the fame of the Superior Being who grew tall and measured the earth, —
we announce our Pāvai[-vow] and bathe for [it]
it will rain three times a month in the whole land without [doing any] harm
and unending prosperity will increase
so that the kayal-fish will leap about among the large superior paddy that grows high
so that the sparkling bees will lie down in the pretty blue nelumbo flowers
so that the fat, generous cows will fill pots
as [the cowherd] enters [the shed] without delay
sits down, catches [hold of] the[ir] excellent dugs and give [them] a pull
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!

ta: ஆழி மழைக் கண்ணா ஒன்று நீ கை கரவேல்
ஊழி முதல்வன் உருவம் போல் மெய் கறுத்துப்
ஆழி போல் மின்னி வலம்புரி போல் நின்றதிர்ந்து
தாழாதே சார்ங்க முதைத்த சர மழை போல்
en: O protector of the rains [resembling] the ocean!
Do not hide back anything!
Entering the ocean, drawing [its water], thundering, climbing up
with the body growing dark like the hue of the Primordial Being
emitting lightning like the discus and always resounding like the rightward curling conch
[that are] in the hands of Padmanābha with wide, beautiful shoulders
May you pour [rains] without delaying in [this] world
like the showers of arrows discharged by Śārṅga
so that [the world] lives and
so that we too [may] rejoicingly bathe for the Mārkaḻi [vow]
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!

ta: தூயோமாய் வந்து நாம் தூமலர் தூவித் தொழுது
en: As we come purified
worshipping by bestrewing pure flowers
singing thanks to [our] mouths [and] thinking thanks to [our] minds
of the Black One
the young Man from northern Mathurā, where He remains [forever]
Him who resides on the banks of the pure Yamunā of abundant waters
the beautiful Light that appeared in the cowherd caste
Dāmodara who enlightened [His] mother’s womb
[our] past sins and the ones that wait to approach [us]
will become [like] cotton [caught] in fire
Say [it]
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, accusative
participial noun, third person, noun, plural

en: See, the birds too have [started to] chirp!
Have you not heard the great sound of the white summoning conch
at the temple of the lord of the birds (Garuḍa)?
O girl, do get up!
The great sound of the hermits and the ascetics saying ‘Hari’
—getting up slowly
keeping in [their] hearts
the Cause that remained asleep on the snake upon the sea waves
having thrust [His] feet into the fake cart so that [its] joints were destroyed
and eaten poison from the demoness’s breasts—
enters [our] hearts [and] cools [it]
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, third person, noun, plural

ta: கீசு கீசென்று எங்கும் ஆனைச் சாத்தான் கலந்து
en: O foolish girl! Have you not heard
chirpings everywhere
the sound of the talks uttered by the meeting king crows?
Have you not heard the sound of curd[-making]
as the cowherdesses, with [their] hair fragrant with aromatic products
move their arms, making noise with the churning staff
so that the kācu- and the piṟappu- necklaces tinkle?
O chief among girls! Are you [still] lying down
even after hearing [our] singing about Nārāyaṇa, Keśava, [our] Lord?
Open [the door], O lustrous [girl]!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: necklace of small seed-like gold pieces
participial noun, second person, singular, vocative

ta: கீழ் வானம் வெள்ளென்று எருமை சிறு வீடு
en: As the eastern sky has dawned
the buffaloes, [being] let out briefly in the morning, have spread out to graze, look!
We have come and stood [here] to summon you
Keeping back the remaining girls who are going, intent upon going on [to bathe]
O joyful lady, do get up!
If, singing and obtaining a paṟai-drum
we go and worship
Him who split [open] the horse’s jaws
the Lord of the gods who destroyed the wrestlers
[He will] bless [us]
having examined [our demands] saying ‘ā! ā!’
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, noun, plural
participial noun, third person, masculine, singular, accusative

ta: கீழ் வானம் வெள்ளென்று எருமை சிறு வீடு
en: O uncle’s daughter who sleep on the bed
as lamps shine all around the mansion [studded with] pure gems
as the incense emits fragrance
Do open the latch of the door [made of] gems!
O aunt, will you not wake her up? Is your daughter mute or deaf or asleep?
Is she kept under guard [or] caught in the spell of the great slumber?
[We] have sung all the many names, saying again and again
‘the great Dark [Lord]! Mādhava! [The Lord] from Vaikuṇṭha!’
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, noun, plural
participial noun, third person, masculine, singular, accusative

ta: போற்றப் பறை தரும் புண்ணியனால் பண்டொரு நாள்
en: O lady entering heaven having practised austerities!
Won’t those who do not open the door even give a reply?
Did Kumbhakarṇa himself
—who, one day in the past, fell into the mouth of death
thanks to the Holy [Lord]
He who will give [us] the paṟai-drum being praised by us
Nārāyaṇa with hair [adorned with] fragrant basil—
give great sleep all to yourself, having lost [to you]?
O you who sleep excessively! O precious ornament!
With a clearness [of mind], come and open [the door]!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

ta: முற்றம் புகுந்து முகில் வண்ணன் பேர் பாட
en: O golden creeper belonging to
the cowherds devoid of a single blemish
who, having milked many herds of milch cows with calves
go and make war so that the enemies’ valour is destroyed!
O peahen from the uplands
whose waist is [akin to] a snake from an ant-hill! Come!
As all the female friends from among the relatives
have come and entered your courtyard
and sung the glory of the cloud-hued [Lord]
oh, what is the meaning of your sleeping
without being perplexed [nor] speaking?
O cherished woman!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!

ta: நினைத்து முலை வழியே நின்று பால் சோர
பனித் தலை வீழ நின் வாசற் கடை பற்றிச்
en: O sister of the good, wealthy man
whose house the buffaloes with young calves drench [and] turn into slush
having bellowed, thought of [and] been distressed for the calves
as milk exudes through the[ir] udders!
You will not open [your] mouth
[even] as we
holding the entrance gate as dew falls on [our] heads
sing [about]
Him who is sweet to the manas
who destroyed the king of Laṅkā in the South out of anger!
Get up at least now! What is this great slumber?
The people from all the houses [here] have learnt [about it]!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

ta: கிள்ளிக் களைந்தானைக் கீர்த்தி மை பாடிப் போய்ப்
பள்ளிக் கிடத்தியோ. பாவாய். நீ நன் னாளால்
en: Heading towards the meeting-place [for] the pāvai-vow
All the girls have reached [it], singing the glories
of Him who split [open] the bird’s beak
of Him who nipped off and weeded out the evil Rākṣasa
Venus has risen, Jupiter has gone to sleep
See, even the birds are chirping
O girl with lotus eyes [that resemble] the deer’s!
O girl! Have you been staying in bed without bathing
diving deep [in the water] so that it is intensely cold?
Oh, on this good day, avoiding deception, join [us]
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular, accusative
participial noun, third person, masculine, singular, accusative
perfective aspect, third person, noun, singular
perfective aspect, third person, noun, plural
pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative

ta: செங்கழுனீர் வாய் நெகிழ்ந்தாம்பல் வாய் கூம்பின காண்
en: Inside the well of your backyard garden
the ceṅkaḻunīr-flowers have opened up
and the water-lilies have closed, see!
The white-toothed ascetics with clothes [the hue of] brick dust
are going to blow the conch of their sacred temple
O lady who said you would wake us up first!
Get up, O shameless [girl], who have [the gift of] the gab!
Sing [about]
Him with lotus eyes [and] big arms
who holds the discus along with the conch
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: participial noun, vocative, singular, second person
pronominalised noun, masculine singular, third person

ta: வல்லை யுன் கட்டுரைகள் பண்டே யுன் வாய் அறிதும்
en: ‘Hey, you, young parrot! Are you still asleep?’
‘Do not call out shrilly, O ladies! I am coming!’
‘[We] know of old [about] your gab [and] falsehood
—[of] you [who are] skilled [in words]!’
‘You are the skilled ones, [but] let it be me!’
‘You come quickly! What is special about you?’
‘Have all [the girls] come?’
‘They have come, [you] come [out] [and] count [for] yourself!
Sing [about] Him who killed the mighty elephant [and]
who is capable of destroying the enmity/the strength in the enemies, the Black One.’
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, second person, masculine, singular

ta: வாயில் காப்பானே. மணிக் கதவம் தாள் திறவாய்
மாயன் மணி வண்ணன் நென்னலே வாய் நேர்ந்தான்
வாயால் முன்னம் முன்னம் மாற்றாதே அம்மா. நீ
en: O guardian of Chief Nandagopa’s palace!
O guardian of the entrance with festoons, where the flag appears!
Please unlock the door [made with] gems!
Yesterday itself, the Black [Lord], the sapphire-hued One
promised to bestow the beating drum on us cowherd girls
We have come purifying ourselves
In order to sing, so that [He] wakes up from sleep
O Lord, do not refuse with your mouth right at the beginning!
You open the loving door fixed on a frame!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: O our lord Nandagopāla who makes the gift of clothes, water [and] food!
do get up!
O tender twig among all those twig-like [women]! O light of the lineage!
O our lady, Yaśodā! do wake up!
O King of the celestials who rose hight and measured the world
cutting through the sky
do not sleep, do get up!
O Baladeva, O lord with feet wearing anklets made of red gold!
[May] your younger Brother and you not sleep!
O our maidens, consider [this] attentively!

ta: உந்து மத களிற்றன் ஓடாத தோள் வலியன்
பந்தல் மேல் பல் கால் குயிலினங்கள் கூவின காண்
பந்தார் விரலி உன் மைத்துனன் பேர் பாடச்
en: O daughter-in-law of
Nandagopāla, who possesses elephants oozing out must
he with strong , unconquered shoulders
O Nappiṉṉai! O woman with hair that emits fragrance!
Open the door
See, the fowl have emerged [from sleep] everywhere and called out!
See, the flocks of koels have cried many times on the pandal of mātavi -creepers
O woman with fingers that hold a ball!
As we sing the glories of your Husband
come and open [the door] rejoicingly, with [your] red-lotus hands
so that [your] bangles filled with beauty resounds!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, feminine, singular
perfective aspect, third person, noun, plural
perfective aspect, third person, noun, plural
pronominalised noun, third person, feminine, singular

ta: குத்து விளக்கெரிய கோட்டுக் கால் கட்டில் மேல்
வைத்துக் கிடந்த மலர் மார்பா வாய் திறவாய்
மைத் தடம் கண்ணினாய் நீ யுன் மணாளனை
en: As the standing lamp shines, O You with a wide chest
Who climbed upon the soft bed with five [qualities], on the cot with ivory legs
and lay placing [Your head] on the breasts of Nappiṉṉai
whose curly hair has blossoms that flower in clusters
open [Your] mouth!
O You with big eyes [coloured with] kohl!
See, you will not allow Your Husband to wake from sleep even for a while!
Oh, you cannot bear separation even for a while!
[This] is not worthy of [Your] nature!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, feminine, singular, vocative

ta: செப்பன்ன மென் முலைச் செவ்வாய்ச் சிறு மருங்குல்
en: O mighty [Lord], who goes ahead of the thirty-three [kinds of] immortals
and removes [their] trembling!
Do wake up [from Your] sleep!
O impartial [Lord]! O strong One!
O faultless One who give fever to the enemies!
Do wake up [from Your] sleep!
O lady Nappiṉṉai with a small waist, red lips, [and] pinnacle-like soft breasts!
O auspicious one!
Do wake up [from Your] sleep!
Giving [us] a circular fan, a metal mirror, and Your Husband
And have us bathe right now!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!

ta: மாற்றாதே பால் சொரியும் வள்ளல் பெரும் பசுக்கள்
மாற்றார் உனக்கு வலி தொலைந்துன் வாசற் கண்
en: O Son of the man who possesses a great [number of]
Big, generous cows that pour down milk without interruption
So that the vessels receiving [it] brim and overflow!
Do wake from sleep!
O [Lord] eager [to protect]! O great One! O Flame that has appeared in [this] world!
Wake up from sleep!
Like the enemies, who, losing [their] arrogance to You
Come to Your doorstep, not [able to] escape
[and] bow at Your feet
We have come worshipping and praising [You]
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, second person, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative

ta: பங்கமாய் வந்து நின் பள்ளிக் கட்டிற் கீழே
கிங்கிணி வாய்ச் செய்த தாமரைப் பூப் போலே
அம் கண் இரண்டும் கொண்டெங்கள் மேல் நோக்குதியேல்
en: Like the kings on the beautiful, spacious, big earth
who, their haughtiness having been defeated
come and gather together beneath Your throne
We have come and approached [You]
Will the red eyes not open on us little by little
Like a lotus flower that resembles the opening of a small bell?
If You look at us with [Your] two beautiful eyes [that open]
like the moon and the sun rise
The curses [that are] on us will come down
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: to open the eyes from sleep

ta: போதருமா போலே நீ பூவைப்பூ வண்ணா வுன்
en: Like the excellent lion—which sleeps
settling down in a mountain cave and lying [there during] the rainy season—
wakes up from sleep
looks with [its] fire-red eyes
moves all around so that its fragrant mane stands on end
shakes [its body]
stretches itself
roars
sets forth
and comes [out]
O bilberry-flower-hued [Lord]!
Graciously come here from Your palace
And sitting on the beautiful throne of surpassing excellence
You grace [us] by looking into the matter for which we have come!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: neuter singular, imperfective aspect, third person
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

ta: சென்றங்குத் தென் இலங்கை செற்றாய் திறல் போற்றி
வென்று பகை கெடுக்கும் நின் கையில் வேல் போற்றி
என்றென்றும் உன் சேவகமே யேத்திப் பறை கொள்வான்
en: ‘O [You] who measured the Earth on that day!
Praised be [Your] feet!
O [You] who, going there, destroyed southern Laṅkā!
Praised be [Your] might!
O [You] who kicked the wheel so that [it] was destroyed!
Praised be [Your] glory!
O [You] who threw the calf as a cudgel!
Praised be [Your] anklets!
O [You] who lifted up the hill [for it] to become an umbrella!
Praised be [Your] qualities!
Praised be the spear in Your hand that destroys the enemies!’
Saying this, we have come today in order to acquire the paṟai-drum
extolling Your valour
[Please] show [us] grace!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
As being born as one woman’s son
[within] a night, You became an[other] woman’s son
and grew up in hiding
[You] caused the design of Kaṃsa—
who, unable to bear [that], intended [you] harm—
to fail
[and] stood as fire in [his] belly, O great Māl!
We have come begging: if [You] give us the paṟai-drum
we shall glorify [Your] wealth worthy of Śrī and [Your] valour
and rejoice, [our] suffering having ended!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, negative, third person

en: O Māl! O sapphire-coloured One!
If You ask [us] what is required for
the rites of the superior people for the Mārkaḻi bathing:
Grant [us]
Conches like Your Pāṅcajanya of a milk-like hue
that sound in such a way that the whole world shakes
Very big, spacious drums
Those who sing ‘pallāṇtu’
Beautiful lamps, flags, canopies
O [You] of the banyan-tree leaf!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: participial noun, third person, noun, plural
participial noun, third person, noun, plural
participial noun, third person, noun, plural
participial noun, third person, noun, plural
participial noun, vocative, singular, second person

ta: பாடிப் பறை கொண்டு யாம் பெறும் சம்மானம்
சூடகமே தோள் வளையே தோடே செவிப் பூவே
ஆடை யுடுப்போம் அதன் பின்னே பாற் சோறு
மூட நெய் பெய்து முழங்கை வழி வாரக்
en: O excellent Govinda who win over the foes!
The rewards that
we [are to] get having sung about You [and]
acquired the paṟai-drums [are]:
bracelets, upper-arm rings, ola rolls, ear-jewels, anklets, and so forth
of a quality praised by world
We shall wear nicely many such jewels; we shall wear garments
After that, we shall stay together and be satisfied
pouring ghee such that it covers the milk-rice
[and] trickles down [our] elbows!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
Going behind the milch cows and reaching the woods
we shall eat together
We have merit enough to have You [take] birth
in the cowherd caste devoid of the least knowledge
O Govinda without a single flaw!
As for [our] relation with You
it will not be destroyed here [even if] we destroy it
Pray do not be angry with us ignorant girls’ calling You
by petty names out of love!
O God! You give [us] paṟai drums!
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!
gloss: participial noun, third person, noun, plural

ta: இற்றைப் பறை கொள்வான் அன்று காண் கோவிந்தா
எற்றைக்கும் ஏழ் ஏழ் பிறவிக்கும் உன் தன்னோடு
en: Listen to the object of [our] coming early in the morning
worshipping You [and] praising Your gold-lotus feet:
Being born in the caste of [people] who subsist by grazing cattle
[You] cannot go without accepting our menial services!
O Govinda! Look, it is not for getting the paṟai-drums [that we have come] today:
We will be devoted to you forever and for [all] fourteen/forty-nine births [to come]!
We shall pay homage only to You!
Change our other desires
O our maidens, accept [and] consider [this] attentively!

ta: அங்கப் பறை கொண்ட வாற்றை யணி புதுவைப்
பைங்கமலத் தண் தெரியல் பட்டர் பிரான் கோதை சொன்ன
en: Those who recite here, in this manner, without fail
all thirty [verses] of the garland [composed] in classical Tamil
spoken by Kōtai—
[daughter of] the head among priests
with cool garlands of fresh lotuses
from the decorated Putuvai—
of the way the auspicious, moon-faced, beautiful-jewel-wearing girls
obtained that paṟai-drum
having gone there [and]
made obeisance to
Keśava
Mādhava who churned the sea [with] ship
shall be gratified
obtaining [His] sacred grace everywhere
thanks to Tirumāl
with red eyes, a beautiful face
[and] four big mountain[-like] shoulders
